title: No one wants to go
hook: one by one the great disciples decline, each remembering being out-argued by him

segments.voice: Yesterday, Vimalakirti lay sick in Vaishali, teaching his visitors that the body is like foam. Your line: the sick layman.

The Buddha asks a simple favor: go and ask after Vimalakirti; he's ill. He turns first to Shariputra, the disciple known for wisdom. And Shariputra says, as the sutra tells it: I'm not fit to go. Then he explains why, with a story about himself coming off badly. The Buddha turns to the next disciple, and the next. Each one says no. Each one has a story, and every story is told by the one who lost the argument.
screen: `A SIMPLE FAVOR.` → `I'M NOT FIT TO GO.` → `EACH ONE HAS A STORY.`

segments.voice: Here are a few of the stories, paraphrased. Shariputra remembers sitting quietly under a tree in the forest, deep in meditation. Vimalakirti came by and told him: that isn't the way to sit. Sit without withdrawing from the world. Sit while doing the ordinary things of life, without leaving behind the people around you. Shariputra had no answer, so he stayed silent. Maudgalyayana remembers teaching a crowd of householders in the street; Vimalakirti stopped him and said the teaching can't be handed out the way he was handing it out. Mahakashyapa remembers going only to poor houses for alms, to give the poor a chance to earn merit. Vimalakirti told him to beg from everyone alike, rich and poor. And then Ananda. The Buddha had been unwell, and Ananda went to a house to fetch some milk. Vimalakirti met him at the door: hush, the Buddha's body is the body of the teaching; don't let anyone hear you say he's sick. Ananda was mortified. Then a voice from the sky said: Ananda, the layman is right. But go and take the milk, and don't be ashamed. Look at what the sutra is doing. These are the great disciples, the names at the center of the older discourses, and each one remembers being out-argued by a householder, and says so in front of everyone. Then even the bodhisattvas decline, Maitreya among them. Each refusal makes the visit sound harder. The sutra is clearing the room for someone.
screen: `SHARIPUTRA UNDER A TREE.` · `KASHYAPA AT THE POOR HOUSES.` · `ANANDA AND THE MILK.` · `THE GREAT DISCIPLES ADMIT IT.` · then, large: `THEY ALL DECLINED.`

segments.voice: Let a memory come of someone getting the better of you in a conversation: a sibling, a teacher, a child whose question stumped you. Notice how it sits in the body, maybe a little heat in the face. Then say to yourself, plainly, as the disciples did: they were right, and I had no answer.
No one wants to go. One by one the Buddha's great disciples decline to visit Vimalakirti, each remembering the day he left them speechless. Today's word.
screen: `NO ONE WANTS TO GO — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: they all declined. Someone is still going to knock on that door. Back tomorrow, same hill.

howItsDone: Some teachers in Mahayana traditions use these refusal stories to teach that practice is not limited to the forest or the meditation hall, and that a layperson's insight can match a monk's.

what a scholar hears: the sutra lets the famous disciples of the older discourses tell stories against themselves, to clear the stage for the bodhisattva Manjushri.

chat.says: Why wouldn't the Buddha's top disciples visit a sick man? That seems rude.
options: Each remembered Vimalakirti out-arguing him once, and said honestly he wasn't fit to go.
They were afraid of catching his illness, so they stayed away to protect the other monks.
The Buddha had told them that householders didn't deserve a visit from his disciples.
chat.meaning: In the sutra, each great disciple declines because Vimalakirti once out-argued him, and each admits it in front of everyone.

Shariputra.meaning: a great disciple of the Buddha, known for wisdom

Maudgalyayana.meaning: one of the Buddha's great disciples

Mahakashyapa.meaning: a great disciple of the Buddha who went begging for alms

Maitreya.meaning: the bodhisattva Buddhists say will be the next Buddha

notes: Paraphrased from the Vimalakirti-nirdesha ch. 3 (the disciples) and ch. 4 (the bodhisattvas); no translation quoted.

Episodes used: Shariputra's sitting in the forest; Maudgalyayana teaching householders; Mahakashyapa begging only from the poor; Ananda and the milk with the voice from the sky. Confirm each, especially the Ananda wording ('the layman is right, but take the milk and don't be ashamed').
Mahakashyapa's reason (to give the poor a chance to earn merit) is the usual reading; confirm.
Hook says each story is told by the one who lost the argument; confirm.

The framing that the sutra lets the older disciples come off badly could read as a polemic against Theravada; it's phrased as the sutra's own move, not a judgment. Keeper should confirm the tone is fair.
howItsDone is a general teaching claim; confirm.
